text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) expects its provisions for the full year 1996 to be somewhat higher as compared to last year, chief financial officer Peter Wuffli said.

Trading volume trends since the end of the third quarter indicated that there may be a slight rebound in the final quarter of this year, but not to levels seen in the first half, Wuffli said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
"That (the provision figure) will be somewhat higher," Wuffli said. But he said in response to a question that the figure would not be so large as to approach a level around 1.5 billion.
"In today's view we don't see that," Wuffli said.
On trading, Wuffli said volumes picked up at the start of the fourth quarter as compared to the third, due in part to several large capital market deals, but he did not specify.
He further stated that during the third quarter, a slowdown was seen in equities participation in the U.K. as well as in Switzerland.
Capital market and corporate finance businesses were also slower, but foreign exchange and interest rate activities remained strong on global basis, he added. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
